text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Officials aligned with Martin Shikuku, secretary general of the opposition FORD-Asili party, warn their chairman against holding grassroot party elections.
- Langata parliamentarian Raila Odinga says the opposition may seek an injunction to stop voter registration unless the period is extended.
- Kenya Posts & Telecommunications is demanding payment of at least 500 million shillings ($9.2 million) in outstanding telephone bills from the government.
- The first national convention for the National Development Party of Kenya will be held tomorrow (Saturday).
- The High Court upholds the expulsion of Kenya National Congress Chairman Chibule wa Tsuma.
- Five councillors defect from opposition Democratic Party of Kenya to the ruling party.
- Seven bishops of the Church of the Province of Kenya (Anglican) are defrocked for their alleged involvement in violence.
- Diplomats from major donor countries hold talks with President Daniel arap Moi expressing concern over the govenment's commitment to hold free and fair elections later this year.

- Taking their cue from a group of Kikuyu elite, a group of wealthy personalities from the Kamba community seek to market the ruling party among the communities amid indications that the opposition may scoop all the votes.
